Our simulated figure is the band this measurement should land in and is stated as an UPPER bound: out/sim-evidence/battery-runtime.json integrates the measured MuJoCo torque and speed profile through ROBOTIS's published XL330 rows and gets 112.7 min of continuous walking at 1.0 W of compute down to 80.4 min at 5.0 W, with pack current 1.3453-1.8859 A at 7.4 V; standing runs 292.94 min down to 143.29 min over the same sweep. That study credits the whole 18.7 Wh, credits no regeneration and takes the PWM stage as loss-free, so the real number must be lower. The compute draw is swept rather than known because NO vendor figure exists: Radxa publishes a 5 V/2 A supply REQUIREMENT and no consumption, and ROBOTIS publishes no no-load current for the XL330-M288-T at any voltage.

tests.title: Empty-battery behaviour
tests.purpose: A biped that runs out of power standing up falls over. This checks that it sits down first.
pre: Either the tail of EN-01, or the servo bus on the bench supply with no pack fitted.
/etc/robot/robotd.toml read and its [safety] block recorded.

steps.do: Read the config this board actually has - the file is not overwritten by updates, so a board provisioned long ago can differ from the release default.
With the robot standing, walk the supply down slowly from 7.400 V toward 6.600 V, no faster than 0.05 V per 10 s.
Read percent against voltage at 8.200, 7.400 and 6.600 V.
Hold at 6.600 V and watch. The EMA moves over about 10 s, so the response is not instant.
steps.expect: the robot sits down gracefully, then powers off

tests.measure: Battery percent at three voltages; the delay between reaching 6.600 V and the sit; whether the sit is controlled; whether the machine powers off.

gate.PASS: percent reads 100 / 50 / 0 at 8.200 / 7.400 / 6.600 V, and at a sustained 6.600 V the robot sits down under control and powers off
gate.FAIL: it keeps standing or walking below 6.600 V, or it drops rather than sits
gate.CD: this board has `battery_empty_shutdown = false` - then the behaviour is correct for its configuration and the unit must not ship that way

tests.gate_basis: `robotd.toml [safety]`, verbatim: 'Sit down gracefully and power the machine off when the battery EMA reaches the empty floor (6.6 V - the same value the battery percentage maps to 0%). The EMA moves over ~10 s, so a load sag cannot trip it; reaching 6.6 requires a genuinely spent pack.' The three percent points are exact, not approximate: model.rs defines BATTERY_FULL_V = 8.2 and BATTERY_EMPTY_V = 6.6 and maps them linearly, and its own test asserts battery_percent(7.4) == 50.0 to within 0.001. Remember what the robot is reading: there is no fuel gauge and no ADC on this design - the only voltage it knows is the servos' `Present Input Voltage(144)`, quantised at 0.1 V per count, which is why EB-06 checks it against a meter.

tests.title: Compute thermal soak, head closed
tests.purpose: The compute sits in a sealed printed head. This is the leg of the thermal problem that a bench can actually measure.
pre: The head is fully closed - shells, face, eye ring, jaw all fitted. A soak with the head open measures nothing.
Room temperature 20-25 degC, recorded.
SN-07 passed.

steps.do: Name the thermal zones before trusting zone 0.
steps.cmd: for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*; do echo "$z $(cat $z/type)"; done

steps.do: Start the load: stream 720p30 to one peer and turn duck detection on at its configured 2 Hz.
steps.cmd: sudo robotctl configure   # [media] quality = 720p30, [detect] enabled = true, hz = 2.0
steps.expect: a stream a viewer can see

steps.do: Every 60 s for 30 minutes, log SoC millidegrees, the current CPU frequency and the fps mediad reports.
Record the plateau, the maximum, and whether the frequency ever sits at 408000.

tests.measure: SoC temperature every minute for 30 minutes; CPU frequency at each sample; the streamed frame rate; room temperature.

gate.PASS: every sample <= 85 degC, `scaling_cur_freq` never pinned at 408000 kHz, and the stream holds >= 29 fps for the whole soak
gate.FAIL: any sample >= 85 degC, or the frequency parks at 408 MHz, or the stream falls below 29 fps
gate.CD: the board exposes no SoC thermal zone - record every zone's `type` and say which was read

tests.gate_basis: 85 degC is the board's own governor threshold, quoted verbatim from the Radxa ZERO 3W product brief §6.5 p.7: 'An internal thermal management governor is in place to regulate these parameters, ensuring that the CPU temperature does not exceed a threshold of 85 degC'. The same page gives the ambient rating: 0 to 50 degC. 408 MHz is not a guess either - it is the MEASURED throttle floor of this SoC on this board, twice in Pollen's own material: media-bringup.md's rotation table records '97 degC, CPU at 408 MHz' with videoflip in the pipeline against '~30 fps, SoC fine' without it, and robotd.toml's [detect] section says of hz = 2.0 that '2 is a thermal limit, not a preference: flat out this reaches 95 degC on a Radxa Zero 3 and the CPU throttles to 408 MHz'. 29 fps is from the same measured line - mediad's 720p30 rung was characterised at 29.3 fps off the ISP main path. Our own enclosure study says why this is the leg that fails: the head holds 194.171 cm3 of still air (56.9 % of its enclosed volume) with no vent, no fan and no heatsink, and the outside skin is NOT the bottleneck - it takes 4.008-17.015 W to lift the skin to the board's 50 degC ambient rating. The missing conduction path is die-to-shell, and no theta_JA is published for the RK3566, so no internal model is asserted here.

tests.title: Head skin temperature after the soak
tests.purpose: What a hand touches, and a proxy for the air the board is breathing inside a closed head.
pre: TH-01 running, at its plateau.
Emissivity set on the instrument and recorded.
tool: IR thermometer with settable emissivity, or a taped K-type thermocouple

steps.do: Set emissivity to 0.95 for matte printed plastic and record the setting with every reading. An IR reading with no emissivity setting is not a temperature.
Sweep the head shell and find the hottest point. Read it three times, 30 s apart.
steps.expect: three readings within 1 degC of each other

steps.do: Record room temperature at the same moment, and the rise above it.

tests.measure: The hottest head-shell temperature, in degC to 1 dp, with the emissivity used; room temperature; the rise.

gate.PASS: hottest head-shell point <= 50.0 degC
gate.FAIL: above 50.0 degC - the air inside the head is hotter than its skin, so a skin at the board's own maximum ambient puts the board past it
gate.CD: the surface is too glossy or too small for the instrument's spot size - use a taped thermocouple instead and say so

tests.gate_basis: The 50.0 degC gate is the BOARD's limit, not a human-comfort limit: Radxa ZERO 3W product brief §6.5 p.7, 'The specified ambient operating temperature for optimal performance of the Radxa ZERO 3W ranges from 0 degC to 50 degC'. The skin is the coolest surface bounding the air the board sits in, so a skin at 50 degC guarantees the board's ambient is above its rating. Our own study puts the expected value far below that: 28.73-39.23 degC for 2.0 W in a 25 degC room, bracketed by the two skin-area estimates and by emissivity 0 and 1 (out/sim-evidence/thermal-compute-head.json). NO touch-temperature safety limit is asserted: the applicable IEC 62368-1 touch-temperature table is not on our shelf, and until it is, this gate speaks for the computer and not for the customer's hand.

open.status: No. The LSM6DSV16X sits behind an unidentified MCU on an unpublished board

open.status: A process gap, not a missing fact. open.status: CANNOT DETERMINE. TH-02 gates at 50.0 degC, which is the Radxa board's own maximum ambient - a limit that speaks for the computer, not for a child's hand on a toy-sized robot. No touch-temperature standard is on our shelf

resolved.q: Which ToF generation ships, VL53L5CX or VL53L8CX?
resolved.was: CANNOT DETERMINE in Rev A - the datasheets were read but nothing said which part is fitted.
resolved.now: SETTLED, and the answer is BOTH. `tof/src/lib.rs` lines 8-11, verbatim: 'Both generations, decided at runtime. The two are interchangeable on the board and differ only in firmware and a driver prefix, so which one is fitted is not a build-time choice: an ID read picks the driver before any firmware is uploaded (Generation). Ducks in the field have both.' The daemon also tries two addresses, 0x29 then 0x52 - 0x29 is the factory default for both generations, and 0x52 is where a prototype moved an L5CX when an I2C IMU wanted 0x29, an address that survives power cycles (tofd/src/main.rs, ADDRESS_CANDIDATES).
resolved.consequence: SN-06 needs no change: the +/- 5 % accuracy figure is identical for both parts at 8x8 / 15 Hz against an 88 % white target, over each datasheet's own far range - 200-4000 mm on the VL53L8CX (DS14161 Rev 12 Table 20, page 26/45) and 201-4000 mm on the VL53L5CX (DS13754 Rev 13 Table 21, page 23/40). Section 3's rail table does: the ToF CORE_1V8 row is N/A rather than FAIL on a unit that came up as a VL53L5CX, because that part has no separate core rail. Record the generation the header names before judging that row.

resolved.q: Is there any test at all for NFC and for the camera-use indicator?
resolved.was: Rev A carried both as 'NO TEST EXISTS' rows - correct about the mechanism, wrong about the observation.
resolved.now: SETTLED for the BEHAVIOUR, still open for the MECHANISM. Pollen ships the NFC stimulus - 10 tags in the Dev Pack, 10 more and an NFC E-Ink 'Polaroid' in the Accessory Pack, which the store page says is tapped on the robot's head - so SN-09 is now a black-box test at each of the two advertised antenna positions. The press kit states the indicator as a shipped feature ('a dedicated camera-use indicator inspired by classic REC lights') and architecture.md §7 states it as a privacy requirement Pollen set itself ('Visible on-robot indicator whenever streaming is active'), so SN-10 is now a three-cycle observation and is on the end-of-line checklist.
resolved.consequence: Neither test asserts a part: no reader IC, no bus, no GPIO. What each CAN catch is a unit that differs from its batch - one antenna dead, or an indicator that does not track the camera.

resolved.q: Does the robot have a second IMU in the head at all?
resolved.was: The overlay called the HAT's BMI088 'dormant, unused but still connected', which reads like a part that might not be fitted.
resolved.now: SETTLED that TWO are fitted. The press-kit spec sheet: 'Motion sensing | 2 IMUs, one in the body and one in the head'. The body one is the imu_to_dxl board at bus ID 200 that robotd sync_reads first every tick.
resolved.consequence: SN-01 through SN-03 stay exactly as they are - what remains open is whether the head part is the HAT's BMI088 and whether any shipped code reads it, which is a different question and is still in the open table below.
